13: # Web Cascade and Selectors
14: 
15: This file keeps the deeper cascade and selector mechanics. The baseline CSS architecture rules remain in [web-markup-and-css.md](web-markup-and-css.md).
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW AND CASCADE AND SPECIFICITY
20: 
21: ### CS1. Cascade decision order
22: 
23: - **Rule:** Resolve competing declarations by origin and importance, layer order, specificity, scope proximity when scoped rules apply, then source order.
24: - **Why:** The cascade compares these criteria in order, so a later rule cannot win by source order when an earlier criterion already decided the result.
25: - **When not to:** Skip the comparison when the declarations do not apply to the same element and property.
26: - **Pitfall:** Normal unlayered declarations outrank normal declarations in named layers, while important declarations reverse layer precedence.
27: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
28: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Cascade
29: 
30: ### CS2. Global cascade layer order
31: 
32: - **Rule:** Declare the cascade layer order once in a global stylesheet before component styles load.
33: - **Why:** Layer order is established the first time each layer name appears. Component style injection can vary with load order, so per-component layer blocks cannot define a reliable shared order.
34: - **When not to:** Use unlayered styles only when the app deliberately relies on the unlayered precedence boundary.
35: - **Pitfall:** A deeply scoped rule inside a layer loses to an unlayered rule even when its selector looks stronger.
36: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-09-14 (web-features `cascade-layers`). Chrome 99 / Firefox 97 / Safari 15.4.
37: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@layer
38: 
39: ### CS3. Specificity arithmetic with Angular emulation
40: 
41: - **Rule:** Count IDs, class-like selectors and type selectors in separate specificity columns before changing a selector.
42: - **Why:** IDs add to the first column, classes, attributes and pseudo-classes add to the second, and type selectors and pseudo-elements add to the third. A component-scoping attribute such as `[data-scope]` adds one class-like unit.
43: - **When not to:** Do not raise specificity when the actual conflict comes from origin, importance or cascade layer order.
44: - **Pitfall:** A selector such as `.card[data-scope]` has specificity `0-2-0`, not `0-1-0`.
45: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
46: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Specificity
47: 
48: ---
49: 
50: ## 2. SELECTOR LOGIC
51: 
52: ### CS4. Zero-specificity and maximum-argument selectors
53: 
54: - **Rule:** Wrap low-priority defaults in `:where()` and use `:is()` when the matching alternatives should share the strongest argument's specificity.
55: - **Why:** `:where()` contributes zero specificity, while `:is()` contributes the specificity of its most specific argument.
56: - **When not to:** Keep a direct class selector when the alternatives would obscure which component states match.
57: - **Pitfall:** Adding a high-specificity selector to one `:is()` alternative raises the specificity of the entire selector.
58: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2023-07-21 (web-features `is`). Chrome 88 / Firefox 82 / Safari 14. Baseline widely available since 2023-07-21 (web-features `where`). Chrome 88 / Firefox 82 / Safari 14.
59: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:is
60: 
61: ### CS5. Narrow relational matching with :has()
62: 
63: - **Rule:** Keep `:has()` selectors narrow and close to the component that owns the matching relationship.
64: - **Why:** The browser reevaluates relational matches as the relevant DOM changes, and a broad ancestor selector can increase style invalidation work.
65: - **When not to:** Prefer an existing direct selector when the relationship is already represented by a simple parent or sibling structure.
66: - **Pitfall:** A broad rule such as `body:has(.is-open)` makes unrelated subtree changes relevant to a page-level selector.
67: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2026-06-19 (web-features `has`). Chrome 105 / Firefox 121 / Safari 15.4.
68: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:has
69: 
70: ---
71: 
72: ## 3. NESTING, SCOPE AND PROPERTIES
73: 
74: ### CS6. Native nesting and the nesting selector
75: 
76: - **Rule:** Use `&` to make the parent selector explicit inside native CSS nesting.
77: - **Why:** The nesting selector represents the full parent selector, so `&:hover` and `.theme &` express relationships without Sass-style string concatenation.
78: - **When not to:** Keep a selector flat when nesting would hide its reach or increase selector complexity.
79: - **Pitfall:** `&-active` does not append a suffix to a class name as it would in Sass.
80: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2026-06-11 (web-features `nesting`). Chrome 120 / Firefox 117 / Safari 17.2.
81: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_nesting/Using_CSS_nesting
82: 
83: ### CS7. Scoped selector boundaries
84: 
85: - **Rule:** Use `@scope` to limit a rule to a component subtree when the required browsers support it.
86: - **Why:** Scoped rules stop at the declared scope boundary, and scope proximity breaks a tie after specificity without changing the selector's specificity.
87: - **When not to:** Use the established component scoping mechanism when a target browser does not support `@scope`.
88: - **Pitfall:** A scope boundary does not prevent unscoped rules from matching the same descendants. In Safari 26.0 through 26.3, rules inside `@scope` do not apply to `<input>` and `<textarea>`; support is complete from 26.4.
89: - **Support:** Baseline newly available since 2026-03-24 (web-features `scope`). Chrome 143 / Firefox 146 / Safari 26.4.
90: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@scope
91: 
92: ### CS8. Registered custom properties
93: 
94: - **Rule:** Register a custom property with `@property` when its type, inheritance behavior or animation behavior must be explicit.
95: - **Why:** Registration gives the browser a syntax, an `inherits` setting and an initial value, which lets typed values interpolate during animation.
96: - **When not to:** Keep an unregistered property when it only carries an inherited token and needs no typed animation.
97: - **Pitfall:** A registered property with the wrong `inherits` value can stop a theme token from reaching its descendants.
98: - **Support:** Baseline newly available since 2024-07-09 (web-features `registered-custom-properties`). Chrome 85 / Firefox 128 / Safari 16.4.
99: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@property
100: 
101: ### CS9. Existing state selector contract
102: 
103: - **Rule:** Follow the state selector contract in [web-markup-and-css.md Section 7](web-markup-and-css.md#7-css-architecture).
104: - **Why:** The web layer already owns how exposed state reaches CSS selectors, so this file does not define a second state source. See [A5](web-accessibility-patterns.md#a5-focus-visible-styling) for the visible keyboard focus rule.
105: - **When not to:** Use a class for a visual-only state that has no semantic state in the markup.
106: - **Pitfall:** A store-owned `.is-open` class can drift from the expanded state already present on the control.
107: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
108: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Attribute_selectors
109:

111:

13: # Web Layout and Sizing
14: 
15: This file keeps the deeper CSS layout mechanics. The baseline flow and responsive rules remain in [web-markup-and-css.md](web-markup-and-css.md).
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW AND STACKING AND CONTAINING BLOCKS
20: 
21: ### L1. Ancestors that capture fixed positioning
22: 
23: - **Rule:** Keep transforms, filters, perspective, paint or layout containment, relevant `will-change` values and `container-type` off ancestors of viewport-fixed headers or bars.
24: - **Why:** These properties can make an ancestor the containing block for a fixed descendant, so the descendant moves with that ancestor instead of the viewport. Transform, filter and containment behavior is longstanding.
25: - **When not to:** Scope a fixed child to an ancestor only when it is meant to remain fixed inside that component.
26: - **Pitfall:** Adding `will-change: transform` to smooth an ancestor can silently change where a fixed child is positioned.
27: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2025-08-14 (web-features `container-queries`). Chrome 105 / Firefox 110 / Safari 16.
28: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Containing_block
29: 
30: ### L2. Stacking context triggers
31: 
32: - **Rule:** Inspect the ancestor chain for a stacking context before increasing a `z-index` value.
33: - **Why:** A stacking context is painted as one unit, so a descendant cannot out-rank content in a different context. Triggers include the root, positioned elements with non-auto `z-index`, fixed or sticky positioning, flex or grid items with `z-index`, opacity below one, blend modes, `transform`, `translate`, `rotate`, `scale`, filters, perspective, clipping, masks, `isolation: isolate`, `contain: layout`, `contain: paint`, `contain: strict`, `contain: content`, `container-type`, `content-visibility: auto` and `will-change` naming one of these properties. Top-layer elements paint above ordinary stacking contexts.
34: - **When not to:** Raise a local `z-index` when the elements already share the same stacking context and the order alone is wrong.
35: - **Pitfall:** An opacity such as `0.999` creates a stacking context, while `isolation: isolate` creates one without changing opacity or clipping paint.
36: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
37: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_positioned_layout/Stacking_context
38: 
39: ### L3. Flow root without clipping
40: 
41: - **Rule:** Use `display: flow-root` to contain floats or stop margin collapse when clipping is not required.
42: - **Why:** A flow root establishes a block formatting context without turning overflow into a clipping or scrolling rule.
43: - **When not to:** Use an overflow value when clipping is an intentional part of the component.
44: - **Pitfall:** `overflow: hidden` can clip content and prevent sticky descendants from sticking to their scrollport.
45: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
46: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_display/Block_formatting_context
47: 
48: ---
49: 
50: ## 2. INTRINSIC AND GRID SIZING
51: 
52: ### L4. Automatic minimum on flex and grid items
53: 
54: - **Rule:** Set `min-width: 0` or `min-inline-size: 0` on a flex or grid child that must shrink below its min-content size.
55: - **Why:** The automatic minimum can preserve the longest unbreakable content width, so the item refuses to shrink to the available track.
56: - **When not to:** Keep the automatic minimum when the item's content must set a lower bound on its track.
57: - **Pitfall:** Setting `overflow: hidden` may hide the overflow while leaving the sizing constraint in place.
58: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
59: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/min-width
60: 
61: ### L5. Grid tracks, subgrid and auto repetition
62: 
63: - **Rule:** Use `minmax(0, 1fr)` when long content must not widen a flexible track, use subgrid when nested items must share parent tracks, and choose `auto-fit` or `auto-fill` by whether empty tracks should collapse.
64: - **Why:** A bare `1fr` has an automatic minimum. Subgrid reuses the parent grid tracks. `auto-fit` collapses empty repeated tracks, while `auto-fill` preserves them.
65: - **When not to:** Keep the intrinsic minimum when content must determine the track size, or use independent tracks when nested columns should not align with the parent.
66: - **Pitfall:** One unbreakable string can widen a grid whose flexible track still has an automatic minimum.
67: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
68: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_grid_layout/Subgrid
69: 
70: ### L6. Container queries and container units
71: 
72: - **Rule:** Put query containment on a wrapper and query from its descendants, then use container units such as `cqi` or `cqw` where sizing should follow that wrapper.
73: - **Why:** A query container cannot use its own size query to style itself. `container-type: inline-size` also establishes containment that can affect fixed descendants and stacking.
74: - **When not to:** Use a viewport media query when the layout decision depends on the viewport rather than the component's available size.
75: - **Pitfall:** Adding `container-type` to the styled component itself does not make that component respond to its own size.
76: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2025-08-14 (web-features `container-queries`). Chrome 105 / Firefox 110 / Safari 16.
77: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_containment/Container_size_and_style_queries
78: 
79: ---
80: 
81: ## 3. MEDIA AND SCROLL GEOMETRY
82: 
83: ### L7. Intrinsic media ratio
84: 
85: - **Rule:** Keep an image's or video's intrinsic `width` and `height` attributes consistent with its CSS `aspect-ratio`.
86: - **Why:** The attributes give the browser a ratio before media loads, while CSS controls the rendered box after styles apply.
87: - **When not to:** Let intrinsic ratio determine the box when the media is not constrained by a fixed layout slot.
88: - **Pitfall:** A conflicting CSS ratio can reserve one shape before load and display another after load.
89: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-03-20 (web-features `aspect-ratio`). Chrome 88 / Firefox 89 / Safari 15.
90: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/aspect-ratio
91: 
92: ### L8. Stable scrollbar space
93: 
94: - **Rule:** Apply `scrollbar-gutter: stable` to the element that owns scrolling when content changes would shift its inline layout.
95: - **Why:** The stable gutter reserves space for a classic scrollbar before overflow appears.
96: - **When not to:** Skip it when the platform uses overlay scrollbars and reserving space would add unwanted width.
97: - **Pitfall:** `stable both-edges` reserves space on both sides and can make a narrow pane needlessly smaller. Without a stable gutter, a classic scrollbar can shift the inline layout.
98: - **Support:** Baseline newly available since 2024-12-11 (web-features `scrollbar-gutter`). Chrome 94 / Firefox 97 / Safari 18.2.
99: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/scrollbar-gutter
100: 
101: ### L9. Scroll chaining and snap points
102: 
103: - **Rule:** Use `overscroll-behavior: contain` on an inner pane that must stop scroll chaining, and use scroll snap only when a destination should settle at defined positions.
104: - **Why:** The contain value keeps overscroll from propagating to an ancestor. Scroll snap adjusts the final scroll position toward configured snap areas.
105: - **When not to:** Keep normal chaining when users should continue scrolling the page after reaching the end of a pane.
106: - **Pitfall:** The `chain` value is unavailable in some browsers. Feature-detect it and keep the default or `contain` path.
107: - **Support:** Baseline limited availability (web-features `overscroll-behavior`). Chrome 144 / Firefox 150 / Safari unsupported. Baseline limited availability (web-features `overscroll-behavior`). Chrome 144 / Firefox 150 / Safari unsupported. Baseline widely available since 2022-07-15 (web-features `scroll-snap`). Chrome 69 / Firefox 68 / Safari 11.
108: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/overscroll-behavior
109: 
110: ### L10. Small, large and dynamic viewport heights
111: 
112: - **Rule:** Choose `svh` for the small visible viewport, `lvh` for the largest viewport and `dvh` when the layout should track browser chrome changes.
113: - **Why:** Mobile browser controls make the visible viewport change. The legacy `vh` behavior corresponds to the large viewport and can extend behind visible browser chrome.
114: - **When not to:** Use a content-driven height when the section should grow with its contents rather than fill a viewport.
115: - **Pitfall:** A `dvh` panel can resize while scrolling, while `lvh` can extend beyond the currently visible area.
116: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
117: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/length#relative_length_units_based_on_viewport
118: 
119: ---
120: 
121: ## 4. INTRINSIC SIZE ENHANCEMENTS
122: 
123: ### L11. Content-sized controls and intrinsic-size animation

13: # Web Layout and Sizing
14: 
15: This file keeps the deeper CSS layout mechanics. The baseline flow and responsive rules remain in [web-markup-and-css.md](web-markup-and-css.md).
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW AND STACKING AND CONTAINING BLOCKS
20: 
21: ### L1. Ancestors that capture fixed positioning
22: 
23: - **Rule:** Keep transforms, filters, perspective, paint or layout containment, relevant `will-change` values and `container-type` off ancestors of viewport-fixed headers or bars.
24: - **Why:** These properties can make an ancestor the containing block for a fixed descendant, so the descendant moves with that ancestor instead of the viewport. Transform, filter and containment behavior is longstanding.
25: - **When not to:** Scope a fixed child to an ancestor only when it is meant to remain fixed inside that component.
26: - **Pitfall:** Adding `will-change: transform` to smooth an ancestor can silently change where a fixed child is positioned.
27: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2025-08-14 (web-features `container-queries`). Chrome 105 / Firefox 110 / Safari 16.
28: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Containing_block
29: 
30: ### L2. Stacking context triggers
31: 
32: - **Rule:** Inspect the ancestor chain for a stacking context before increasing a `z-index` value.
33: - **Why:** A stacking context is painted as one unit, so a descendant cannot out-rank content in a different context. Triggers include the root, positioned elements with non-auto `z-index`, fixed or sticky positioning, flex or grid items with `z-index`, opacity below one, blend modes, `transform`, `translate`, `rotate`, `scale`, filters, perspective, clipping, masks, `isolation: isolate`, `contain: layout`, `contain: paint`, `contain: strict`, `contain: content`, `container-type`, `content-visibility: auto` and `will-change` naming one of these properties. Top-layer elements paint above ordinary stacking contexts.
34: - **When not to:** Raise a local `z-index` when the elements already share the same stacking context and the order alone is wrong.
35: - **Pitfall:** An opacity such as `0.999` creates a stacking context, while `isolation: isolate` creates one without changing opacity or clipping paint.
36: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
37: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_positioned_layout/Stacking_context
38: 
39: ### L3. Flow root without clipping
40: 
41: - **Rule:** Use `display: flow-root` to contain floats or stop margin collapse when clipping is not required.
42: - **Why:** A flow root establishes a block formatting context without turning overflow into a clipping or scrolling rule.
43: - **When not to:** Use an overflow value when clipping is an intentional part of the component.
44: - **Pitfall:** `overflow: hidden` can clip content and prevent sticky descendants from sticking to their scrollport.
45: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
46: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_display/Block_formatting_context
47: 
48: ---
49: 
50: ## 2. INTRINSIC AND GRID SIZING
51: 
52: ### L4. Automatic minimum on flex and grid items
53: 
54: - **Rule:** Set `min-width: 0` or `min-inline-size: 0` on a flex or grid child that must shrink below its min-content size.
55: - **Why:** The automatic minimum can preserve the longest unbreakable content width, so the item refuses to shrink to the available track.
56: - **When not to:** Keep the automatic minimum when the item's content must set a lower bound on its track.
57: - **Pitfall:** Setting `overflow: hidden` may hide the overflow while leaving the sizing constraint in place.
58: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
59: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/min-width
60: 
61: ### L5. Grid tracks, subgrid and auto repetition
62: 
63: - **Rule:** Use `minmax(0, 1fr)` when long content must not widen a flexible track, use subgrid when nested items must share parent tracks, and choose `auto-fit` or `auto-fill` by whether empty tracks should collapse.
64: - **Why:** A bare `1fr` has an automatic minimum. Subgrid reuses the parent grid tracks. `auto-fit` collapses empty repeated tracks, while `auto-fill` preserves them.
65: - **When not to:** Keep the intrinsic minimum when content must determine the track size, or use independent tracks when nested columns should not align with the parent.
66: - **Pitfall:** One unbreakable string can widen a grid whose flexible track still has an automatic minimum.
67: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
68: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_grid_layout/Subgrid
69: 
70: ### L6. Container queries and container units
71: 
72: - **Rule:** Put query containment on a wrapper and query from its descendants, then use container units such as `cqi` or `cqw` where sizing should follow that wrapper.
73: - **Why:** A query container cannot use its own size query to style itself. `container-type: inline-size` also establishes containment that can affect fixed descendants and stacking.
74: - **When not to:** Use a viewport media query when the layout decision depends on the viewport rather than the component's available size.
75: - **Pitfall:** Adding `container-type` to the styled component itself does not make that component respond to its own size.
76: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2025-08-14 (web-features `container-queries`). Chrome 105 / Firefox 110 / Safari 16.
77: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_containment/Container_size_and_style_queries
78: 
79: ---
80: 
81: ## 3. MEDIA AND SCROLL GEOMETRY
82: 
83: ### L7. Intrinsic media ratio
84: 
85: - **Rule:** Keep an image's or video's intrinsic `width` and `height` attributes consistent with its CSS `aspect-ratio`.
86: - **Why:** The attributes give the browser a ratio before media loads, while CSS controls the rendered box after styles apply.
87: - **When not to:** Let intrinsic ratio determine the box when the media is not constrained by a fixed layout slot.
88: - **Pitfall:** A conflicting CSS ratio can reserve one shape before load and display another after load.
89: - **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-03-20 (web-features `aspect-ratio`). Chrome 88 / Firefox 89 / Safari 15.
90: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/aspect-ratio
91: 
92: ### L8. Stable scrollbar space
93: 
94: - **Rule:** Apply `scrollbar-gutter: stable` to the element that owns scrolling when content changes would shift its inline layout.
95: - **Why:** The stable gutter reserves space for a classic scrollbar before overflow appears.
96: - **When not to:** Skip it when the platform uses overlay scrollbars and reserving space would add unwanted width.

99: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/scrollbar-gutter
100: 
101: ### L9. Scroll chaining and snap points
102: 
103: - **Rule:** Use `overscroll-behavior: contain` on an inner pane that must stop scroll chaining, and use scroll snap only when a destination should settle at defined positions.
104: - **Why:** The contain value keeps overscroll from propagating to an ancestor. Scroll snap adjusts the final scroll position toward configured snap areas.
105: - **When not to:** Keep normal chaining when users should continue scrolling the page after reaching the end of a pane.
106: - **Pitfall:** The `chain` value is unavailable in some browsers. Feature-detect it and keep the default or `contain` path.
107: - **Support:** Baseline limited availability (web-features `overscroll-behavior`). Chrome 144 / Firefox 150 / Safari unsupported. Baseline limited availability (web-features `overscroll-behavior`). Chrome 144 / Firefox 150 / Safari unsupported. Baseline widely available since 2022-07-15 (web-features `scroll-snap`). Chrome 69 / Firefox 68 / Safari 11.
108: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/overscroll-behavior
109: 
110: ### L10. Small, large and dynamic viewport heights
111: 
112: - **Rule:** Choose `svh` for the small visible viewport, `lvh` for the largest viewport and `dvh` when the layout should track browser chrome changes.
113: - **Why:** Mobile browser controls make the visible viewport change. The legacy `vh` behavior corresponds to the large viewport and can extend behind visible browser chrome.
114: - **When not to:** Use a content-driven height when the section should grow with its contents rather than fill a viewport.
115: - **Pitfall:** A `dvh` panel can resize while scrolling, while `lvh` can extend beyond the currently visible area.
116: - **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
117: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/length#relative_length_units_based_on_viewport
118:

121: ## 4. INTRINSIC SIZE ENHANCEMENTS

129: - **Support:** Baseline newly available since 2026-06-16 (web-features `field-sizing`). Chrome 123 / Firefox 152 / Safari 26.2. Baseline limited availability (web-features `interpolate-size`). Chrome 129 / Firefox unsupported / Safari unsupported. Baseline limited availability (web-features `calc-size`). Chrome 129 / Firefox unsupported / Safari unsupported.
130: - **See also:** https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/field-sizing

621: 
622: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
623: 
624: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
625: 
626: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
627: 
628: **Decision Criteria**:
629: 
630: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
631: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
632: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
633: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
634: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
635: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
636: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
637: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
638: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
639: 
640: ### Extraction Pattern
641: 
642: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
643: ```markdown
644: ### [Workflow Name]
645: 
646: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
647: 
648: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
649: 
650: **Quick Overview**:
651: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
652: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
653: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
654: 
655: **Configuration Options:**
656: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
657: - Default values optimized for common use cases
658: ```
659: 
660: ### Benefits of Separation
661: 
662: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
663: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
664: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
665: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
666: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
667: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
668: 
669: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
670: 
671: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
672: \```python
673: def detect_mode(request):
674:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
675:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
676:     return 'interactive', 10
677: \```
678: 
679: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
680: 
681: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
682: \```python
683: from dataclasses import dataclass
684: 
685: @dataclass
686: class ModeConfig:
687:     mode: str
688:     depth_rounds: int
689: 
690: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
691:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
692:     if '$quick' in request:
693:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
694:     elif '$ticket' in request:
695:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
696:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
697: \```
698: 
699: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
700: \```python
701: def test_quick_mode():
702:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
703: \```
704: 
705: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
706: 
707: ---
708: 
709: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
710: 
711: ### Purpose
712: 
713: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
714: 
715: **When to use YAML**:
716: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
717: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
718: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
719: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
720: - Validation schemas
721: 
722: ### Standard YAML Structure
723: 
724: ```yaml
725: # [config-name].yaml
726: metadata:
727:   version: "1.0.0"
728:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
729: 
730: config:
731:   threshold_values:
732:     low: 1
733:     medium: 5
734:     high: 10
735:   feature_flags:
736:     enable_feature_x: true
737:   mappings:
738:     $quick: "quick_mode"
739:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
740: ```
741: 
742: ### File Organization
743: 
744: ```
745: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
746: ├── assets/
747: │   ├── workflow-configs/
748: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
749: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
750: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
751: │   ├── mappings/
752: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
753: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
754: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
755: │   └── templates/
756: │       └── [template files]
757: ```
758: 
759: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
760: 
761: ```python
762: import yaml
763: from pathlib import Path
764: 
765: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
766:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
767:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
768:     with open(config_path) as f:
769:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
770: 
771: # Usage
772: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
773: ```
774: 
775: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
776: 
777: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
778: ```markdown
779: | Trigger                    | Action             |
780: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
781: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
782: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
783: ```
784: 
785: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
786: 
787: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
788: ```yaml
789: config:
790:   variant_triggers:
791:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
792:     implicit:
793:       complexity_threshold: 7
794:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
795:   variant_count:
796:     simple: [2, 3]
797:     complex: [5, 10]
798: ```
799: 
800: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
801: ```python
802: import yaml
803: 
804: class VariantDetector:
805:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
806:         with open(config_path) as f:
807:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
808: 
809:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
810:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
811:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
812:             return True
813: 
814:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
815:         if complexity >= threshold:
816:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
817:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
818:         return False
819: ```
820: 
821: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
822: 
823: ---
824: 
825: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
826: 
827: ### When to Use Python for Logic
828: 
829: **Use Python scripts when**:
830: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
831: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
832: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
833: - API integration (external services)
834: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
835: 
836: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
837: 
838: **Always include**:
839: - Type hints for parameters and return values
840: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
841: - Dataclasses for structured data
842: 
843: **Example**:
844: ```python
845: from dataclasses import dataclass
846: from pathlib import Path
847: 
848: @dataclass
849: class ValidationResult:
850:     is_valid: bool
851:     errors: list[str]
852: 
853: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
854:     """
855:     Validate configuration file.
856: 
857:     Args:
858:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
859: 
860:     Returns:
861:         ValidationResult with status and errors
862: 
863:     Raises:
864:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
865:     """
866:     if not config_path.exists():
867:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
868:     # Validation logic
869:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
870: ```
871: 
872: ### Unit Testing Requirements
873: 
874: **Every Python script must have tests**:
875: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
876: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
877: - Framework: pytest
878: 
879: **Example**:
880: ```python
881: import pytest
882: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
883: 
884: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
885:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
886:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
887:     result = validate_config(config)
888:     assert result.is_valid
889: 
890: def test_validate_missing_file():
891:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
892:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
893: ```
894: 
895: ### Import and Reference Patterns
896: 
897: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
898: 
899: **Markdown references**:
900: ```markdown
901: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
902: ```
903: 
904: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
905: 
906: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
907: ```markdown
908: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
909: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
910: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
911: ```
912: 
913: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
914: 
915: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
916: ```python
917: from typing import Literal
918: from dataclasses import dataclass
919: 
920: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
921: 
922: @dataclass
923: class WorkflowDecision:
924:     mode: WorkflowMode
925:     depth_rounds: int
926: 
927: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
928:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
929:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
930:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
931:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
932:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
933:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
934: ```
935: 
936: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
937: ```python
938: def test_quick_mode():
939:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
940: 
941: def test_default_mode():
942:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
943: ```
944: 
945: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
946: 
947: ---
948: 
949: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
950: 
951: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
952: 
953: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
954: 
955: ```
956: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
957: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
958: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
959: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
960: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
961: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
962: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
963: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
964: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
965: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
966: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
967: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
968: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
969: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
970: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
971: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
972: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
973: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
974: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
975: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
976: │       ├── template-name.md
977: │       └── component-template.tsx
978: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
979:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
980:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
981:     ├── test_config_validator.py
982:     └── __init__.py
983: ```
984: 
985: ### Directory Purposes
986: 
987: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
988: 
989: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
990: 
991: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
992: 
993: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
994: 
995: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
996: 
997: ### When to Create Each Directory
998: 
999: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1000: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1001: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1002: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1003: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1004: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1005: 
1006: ### Integration Pattern
1007: 
1008: **How components work together:**
1009: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1010: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1011: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1012: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"
1013:

54: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE

56: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro

58: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**

64: trigger_phrases:

See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.

150: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
151: 
152: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
153: 
154: **Core Purpose**:
155: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
156: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
157: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
158: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
159: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
160: 
161: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
162: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
163: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
164: 
165: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
166: 
167: ```
168: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
169:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
170:             ↓
171: Level 2: SKILL.md body
172:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
173:             ↓
174: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
175:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)

622: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
623: 
624: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
625: 
626: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
627: 
628: **Decision Criteria**:
629: 
630: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
631: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
632: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
633: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
634: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
635: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
636: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
637: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
638: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
639: 
640: ### Extraction Pattern
641: 
642: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
643: ```markdown
644: ### [Workflow Name]
645: 
646: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
647: 
648: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
649: 
650: **Quick Overview**:
651: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
652: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
653: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
654: 
655: **Configuration Options:**
656: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
657: - Default values optimized for common use cases
658: ```
659: 
660: ### Benefits of Separation
661: 
662: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
663: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
664: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
665: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
666: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
667: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
668: 
669: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
670: 
671: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
672: \```python
673: def detect_mode(request):
674:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
675:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
676:     return 'interactive', 10
677: \```
678: 
679: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
680: 
681: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
682: \```python
683: from dataclasses import dataclass
684: 
685: @dataclass
686: class ModeConfig:
687:     mode: str
688:     depth_rounds: int
689: 
690: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
691:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
692:     if '$quick' in request:
693:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
694:     elif '$ticket' in request:
695:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
696:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
697: \```
698: 
699: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
700: \```python
701: def test_quick_mode():
702:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
703: \```
704: 
705: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
706:

709: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
710: 
711: ### Purpose
712: 
713: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
714: 
715: **When to use YAML**:
716: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
717: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
718: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
719: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
720: - Validation schemas
721: 
722: ### Standard YAML Structure
723: 
724: ```yaml
725: # [config-name].yaml
726: metadata:
727:   version: "1.0.0"
728:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
729: 
730: config:
731:   threshold_values:
732:     low: 1
733:     medium: 5
734:     high: 10
735:   feature_flags:
736:     enable_feature_x: true
737:   mappings:
738:     $quick: "quick_mode"
739:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
740: ```
741: 
742: ### File Organization
743: 
744: ```
745: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
746: ├── assets/
747: │   ├── workflow-configs/
748: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
749: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
750: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
751: │   ├── mappings/
752: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
753: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
754: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
755: │   └── templates/
756: │       └── [template files]
757: ```
758: 
759: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
760: 
761: ```python
762: import yaml
763: from pathlib import Path
764: 
765: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
766:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
767:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
768:     with open(config_path) as f:
769:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
770: 
771: # Usage
772: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
773: ```
774: 
775: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
776: 
777: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
778: ```markdown
779: | Trigger                    | Action             |
780: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
781: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
782: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
783: ```
784: 
785: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
786: 
787: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
788: ```yaml
789: config:
790:   variant_triggers:
791:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
792:     implicit:
793:       complexity_threshold: 7
794:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
795:   variant_count:
796:     simple: [2, 3]
797:     complex: [5, 10]
798: ```
799: 
800: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
801: ```python
802: import yaml
803: 
804: class VariantDetector:
805:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
806:         with open(config_path) as f:
807:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
808: 
809:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
810:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
811:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
812:             return True
813: 
814:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
815:         if complexity >= threshold:
816:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
817:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
818:         return False
819: ```
820: 
821: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible

825: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
826: 
827: ### When to Use Python for Logic
828: 
829: **Use Python scripts when**:
830: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
831: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
832: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
833: - API integration (external services)
834: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
835: 
836: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
837: 
838: **Always include**:
839: - Type hints for parameters and return values
840: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
841: - Dataclasses for structured data
842: 
843: **Example**:
844: ```python
845: from dataclasses import dataclass
846: from pathlib import Path
847: 
848: @dataclass
849: class ValidationResult:
850:     is_valid: bool
851:     errors: list[str]
852: 
853: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
854:     """
855:     Validate configuration file.
856: 
857:     Args:
858:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
859: 
860:     Returns:
861:         ValidationResult with status and errors
862: 
863:     Raises:
864:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
865:     """
866:     if not config_path.exists():
867:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
868:     # Validation logic
869:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
870: ```
871: 
872: ### Unit Testing Requirements
873: 
874: **Every Python script must have tests**:
875: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
876: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
877: - Framework: pytest
878: 
879: **Example**:
880: ```python
881: import pytest
882: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
883: 
884: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
885:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
886:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
887:     result = validate_config(config)
888:     assert result.is_valid
889: 
890: def test_validate_missing_file():
891:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
892:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
893: ```
894: 
895: ### Import and Reference Patterns
896: 
897: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
898: 
899: **Markdown references**:
900: ```markdown
901: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
902: ```
903: 
904: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
905: 
906: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
907: ```markdown
908: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
909: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
910: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
911: ```
912: 
913: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
914: 
915: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
916: ```python
917: from typing import Literal
918: from dataclasses import dataclass
919: 
920: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
921: 
922: @dataclass
923: class WorkflowDecision:
924:     mode: WorkflowMode
925:     depth_rounds: int
926: 
927: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
928:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
929:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
930:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
931:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
932:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
933:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
934: ```
935: 
936: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
937: ```python
938: def test_quick_mode():
939:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
940: 
941: def test_default_mode():
942:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
943: ```

969: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions

978: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests

981:     ├── test_config_validator.py
982:     └── __init__.py

987: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines

989: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**

# Web Markup and CSS Practice

The web layer for the frontend practice core, with framework examples kept beside the platform rules they express.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW AND BOUNDARY

This file is the web layer of [`frontend-practice.md`](frontend-practice.md). It expresses all eleven core principles through web markup, forms, layout, responsive behavior, media and framework patterns.

This file owns web mechanics. It does not own:

- **Values.** Use the project's installed tokens and report a missing token, as [core principle 7](frontend-practice.md#2-the-eleven-principles) requires. When the tokens or the frame leave a value open, use [sk-design-fundamentals](../../../sk-design/sk-design-fundamentals/SKILL.md) for guidance.
- **Interaction details.** Form behavior, touch and hit areas, typography implementation, focus and keyboard behavior, motion, performance and feedback are in [`interaction-craft.md`](../../../sk-design/sk-design-fundamentals/references/interaction-craft.md) Sections 2–8. This file links to them and does not repeat their detail.
- **Figma translation.** The shared rules and five-pass check are in [`figma-to-code.md`](figma-to-code.md) and [core Section 4](frontend-practice.md#4-figma-as-reference).
- **The project's own conventions.** A project or stack mode may replace, extend or disable one core or stack-layer statement for its surface. Follow the core's [overrides rule](frontend-practice.md#5-overrides). The mode declares its choice under a Frontend overrides heading in its own SKILL.md.
- **Visual direction.** A frame records appearance and states. Resolve values the frame and installed tokens leave open through [sk-design-fundamentals](../../../sk-design/sk-design-fundamentals/SKILL.md).

---

## 2. STRUCTURE AND SEMANTICS

- Use landmarks: one `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>` and `<footer>` per page shell, and `<aside>` or `<section>` with a heading for distinct regions.
- Use one `<h1>` per page. Choose heading levels by the document outline, never by visual size. Type size comes from a type token.
- Use `<button>` for an action and `<a href>` for navigation, as [core principle 1](frontend-practice.md#2-the-eleven-principles) requires. A clickable `<div>` or `<span>` has no keyboard support, role or disabled state.
- Give every `<button>` inside a `<form>` an explicit `type`: `type="button"` unless it submits the form.
- Use `<ul>` or `<ol>` for lists of things, and `<table>` for tabular data with a `<caption>` and `<th scope="col">` or `<th scope="row">`. Do not build a data grid from nested `div`s when a table fits.
- Use native elements before ARIA: `<dialog>`, `<details>` and `<summary>`, `<select>` or `<input type="checkbox">`. ARIA fills a gap the platform leaves. It does not replace an available native element.
- Give a custom widget its state with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` on a disclosure trigger, `aria-current="page"` on the active navigation link, `aria-selected` in a tablist and `aria-live="polite"` on a region whose text changes without a page load. This expresses [core principle 2](frontend-practice.md#2-the-eleven-principles).
- Set `lang` on `<html>` and on any inline passage in another language.
- Hide content with the `hidden` attribute. Make a background region non-interactive with `inert` while a modal is open.
- Use a visually hidden utility class for text meant only for screen readers. Do not use `display: none` or `visibility: hidden`, which also hide the text from assistive technology.

**Deeper:** [Elements and attributes](web-elements-and-attributes.md) and [accessibility patterns](web-accessibility-patterns.md).

---

## 3. FORMS

Form behavior such as label focus, the form wrapper, input `type`, `required`, decorations and double submits is in [`interaction-craft.md`](../../../sk-design/sk-design-fundamentals/references/interaction-craft.md) Section 2. The web markup adds these requirements. It expresses [core principles 2 and 3](frontend-practice.md#2-the-eleven-principles):

- Give every control a visible label with `<label for="id">` or a wrapping `<label>`. A placeholder is not a label.
- Group related controls in `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`. Radio and checkbox groups require this context.
- Give every control a `name`, so the form serializes and autofill can match it.
- Set `inputmode` (`numeric`, `decimal`, `email`, `tel`, `url` or `search`) to choose the right mobile keyboard. Set `enterkeyhint` (`next`, `done`, `search` or `send`) when the Enter key has a specific action.
- Link help and error text with `aria-describedby`. Set `aria-invalid="true"` while a control has an error.
- Use native constraints (`required`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `pattern` and `maxlength`) so the browser validates before the app.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# COMPONENT: README/DOCUMENTATION FORMAT VALIDATOR
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

"""
README/Documentation Format Validator

Validates markdown documentation against template rules to ensure
consistent formatting with proper TOC, H2 emojis, and section structure.

Usage:
    python validate_document.py <document.md> [--type readme|code_folder|skill|reference|asset|agent|command|install_guide|security_policy|skill_router|spec|changelog]
    python validate_document.py <document.md> --json
    python validate_document.py <document.md> --fix [--dry-run]
    python validate_document.py <document.md> --blocking-only

Exit Codes:
    0 - Valid (no blocking errors)
    1 - Invalid (blocking errors found)
    2 - File not found or parse error

Citation drift advisory:
    The human report ends with any `cite-drift advisory:` lines that
    cite-drift-scan.mjs --advise prints for the document's file-and-line
    citations. They never change the exit code, and --json and
    --blocking-only skip them. JEV_FEATURE_CITE_DRIFT=0 and JEV_FEATURES=0
    skip the check, as does the older SKDOC_CITE_DRIFT_CHECK=0;
    SKDOC_CITE_DRIFT_OUT=<dir> records its model calls in <dir>/calls.jsonl.

Examples:
    python validate_document.py README.md
    python validate_document.py SKILL.md --type skill
    python validate_document.py doc.md --json
    python validate_document.py doc.md --fix --dry-run
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple


# Command frontmatter shares its description-budget, quote handling, and MCP-token
# rules with the sibling skill validator so the two never diverge on the same
# frontmatter. The sibling lives next to this file; fall back to local copies only if
# it cannot be imported, so this validator always stays runnable on its own.
try:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
    from quick_validate import (  # type: ignore
        check_description_length as _check_description_length,
        strip_matching_quotes as _strip_matching_quotes,
        is_non_fq_mcp_token as _is_non_fq_mcp_token,
        iter_allowed_tools as _iter_allowed_tools,
        DESCRIPTION_SOFT_TARGET_COMMAND as _DESC_SOFT_COMMAND,
        DESCRIPTION_HARD_CAP as _DESC_HARD_CAP,
    )
except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive fallback if the sibling is unavailable
    _DESC_SOFT_COMMAND, _DESC_HARD_CAP = 110, 1536

    def _strip_matching_quotes(value: str) -> str:
        value = value.strip()
        if len(value) >= 2 and value[0] == value[-1] and value[0] in ('"', "'"):
            return value[1:-1]
        return value

    def _check_description_length(description, soft_target, hard_cap=_DESC_HARD_CAP):
        length = len(description)
        if length > hard_cap:
            return (
                f"Description is {length} chars, exceeds hard cap of {hard_cap} chars.",
                None,
            )
        if length > soft_target:
            return (None, f"Description is {length} chars, exceeds soft target of {soft_target}.")
        return (None, None)

    _MCP_NAMESPACE_RE = re.compile(r'^mcp_', re.IGNORECASE)
    _MCP_FQ_RE = re.compile(
        r'^mcp__[a-z0-9]+(?:[_-][a-z0-9]+)*__(?:\*|[a-z0-9]+(?:[_-][a-z0-9]+)*)$',
        re.IGNORECASE,
    )

    def _is_non_fq_mcp_token(token: str) -> bool:
        token = token.strip()
        return bool(_MCP_NAMESPACE_RE.match(token)) and not bool(_MCP_FQ_RE.match(token))

    def _iter_allowed_tools(tools_value: str):
        value = tools_value.strip()
        if value.startswith('[') and value.endswith(']'):
            value = value[1:-1]
        for token in value.split(','):
            token = token.strip()
            if token:
                yield token


# PyYAML ships with the system interpreter but not with every Homebrew install, so
# the frontmatter parse stays optional: without it, a line check still catches the
# common shapes a strict parser rejects and a key-by-key reader does not.

# Web Cascade and Selectors

This file keeps the deeper cascade and selector mechanics.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

It covers CSS cascade order, selector specificity and modern selector behavior.

### When to Use

- Changing how competing declarations resolve across origin, cascade layers, specificity and source order.
- Rewriting a selector that relies on `:is()`, `:where()` or `:has()` matching, or on a specificity calculation.
- Adding native nesting or an `@scope` boundary to existing selectors.
- Registering a custom property with `@property`.

### Boundaries

- **Baseline CSS architecture.** The baseline CSS architecture rules remain in [web-markup-and-css.md](web-markup-and-css.md).
- **State selectors.** The state selector contract is owned by [web-markup-and-css.md Section 7](web-markup-and-css.md#7-css-architecture), and the visible keyboard focus rule by [web-accessibility-patterns.md A5](web-accessibility-patterns.md#a5-focus-visible-styling).

---

## 2. CASCADE AND SPECIFICITY

### CS1. Cascade decision order

- **Rule:** Resolve competing declarations by origin and importance, layer order, specificity, scope proximity when scoped rules apply, then source order.
- **Why:** The cascade compares these criteria in order, so a later rule cannot win by source order when an earlier criterion already decided the result.
- **When not to:** Skip the comparison when the declarations do not apply to the same element and property.
- **Pitfall:** Normal unlayered declarations outrank normal declarations in named layers, while important declarations reverse layer precedence.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [MDN: CSS cascade](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Cascade)

### CS2. Global cascade layer order

- **Rule:** Declare the cascade layer order once in a global stylesheet before component styles load.
- **Why:** Layer order is established the first time each layer name appears. Component style injection can vary with load order, so per-component layer blocks cannot define a reliable shared order.
- **When not to:** Use unlayered styles only when the app deliberately relies on the unlayered precedence boundary.
- **Pitfall:** A deeply scoped rule inside a layer loses to an unlayered rule even when its selector looks stronger.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2024-09-14 (web-features `cascade-layers`). Chrome 99 / Firefox 97 / Safari 15.4.
- **See also:** [MDN: CSS cascade layers (@layer)](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@layer)

### CS3. Specificity arithmetic

- **Rule:** Count IDs, class-like selectors and type selectors in separate specificity columns before changing a selector.
- **Why:** IDs add to the first column, classes, attributes and pseudo-classes add to the second, and type selectors and pseudo-elements add to the third. A component-scoping attribute such as `[data-scope]` adds one class-like unit.
- **When not to:** Do not raise specificity when the actual conflict comes from origin, importance or cascade layer order.
- **Pitfall:** A selector such as `.card[data-scope]` has specificity `0-2-0`, not `0-1-0`.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [MDN: CSS specificity](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Specificity)

---

## 3. SELECTOR LOGIC

### CS4. Zero-specificity and maximum-argument selectors

- **Rule:** Wrap low-priority defaults in `:where()` and use `:is()` when the matching alternatives should share the strongest argument's specificity.
- **Why:** `:where()` contributes zero specificity, while `:is()` contributes the specificity of its most specific argument.
- **When not to:** Keep a direct class selector when the alternatives would obscure which component states match.
- **Pitfall:** Adding a high-specificity selector to one `:is()` alternative raises the specificity of the entire selector.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2023-07-21 (web-features `is`). Chrome 88 / Firefox 82 / Safari 14. Baseline widely available since 2023-07-21 (web-features `where`). Chrome 88 / Firefox 82 / Safari 14.
- **See also:** [MDN: :is()](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:is)

### CS5. Narrow relational matching with :has()

- **Rule:** Keep `:has()` selectors narrow and close to the component that owns the matching relationship.
- **Why:** The browser reevaluates relational matches as the relevant DOM changes, and a broad ancestor selector can increase style invalidation work.
- **When not to:** Prefer an existing direct selector when the relationship is already represented by a simple parent or sibling structure.
- **Pitfall:** A broad rule such as `body:has(.is-open)` makes unrelated subtree changes relevant to a page-level selector.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2026-06-19 (web-features `has`). Chrome 105 / Firefox 121 / Safari 15.4.
- **See also:** [MDN: :has()](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:has)

---

## 4. NESTING, SCOPE AND PROPERTIES

### CS6. Native nesting and the nesting selector

- **Rule:** Use `&` to make the parent selector explicit inside native CSS nesting.
- **Why:** The nesting selector represents the full parent selector, so `&:hover` and `.theme &` express relationships without Sass-style string concatenation.
- **When not to:** Keep a selector flat when nesting would hide its reach or increase selector complexity.
- **Pitfall:** `&-active` does not append a suffix to a class name as it would in Sass.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2026-06-11 (web-features `nesting`). Chrome 120 / Firefox 117 / Safari 17.2.
- **See also:** [MDN: Using CSS nesting](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_nesting/Using_CSS_nesting)

### CS7. Scoped selector boundaries

- **Rule:** Use `@scope` to limit a rule to a component subtree when the required browsers support it.
- **Why:** Scoped rules stop at the declared scope boundary, and scope proximity breaks a tie after specificity without changing the selector's specificity.
- **When not to:** Use the established component scoping mechanism when a target browser does not support `@scope`.
- **Pitfall:** A scope boundary does not prevent unscoped rules from matching the same descendants. In Safari 26.0 through 26.3, rules inside `@scope` do not apply to `<input>` and `<textarea>`; support is complete from 26.4.
- **Support:** Baseline newly available since 2026-03-24 (web-features `scope`). Chrome 143 / Firefox 146 / Safari 26.4.
- **See also:** [MDN: CSS @scope](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@scope)

### CS8. Registered custom properties

- **Rule:** Register a custom property with `@property` when its type, inheritance behavior or animation behavior must be explicit.
- **Why:** Registration gives the browser a syntax, an `inherits` setting and an initial value, which lets typed values interpolate during animation.
- **When not to:** Keep an unregistered property when it only carries an inherited token and needs no typed animation.
- **Pitfall:** A registered property with the wrong `inherits` value can stop a theme token from reaching its descendants.
- **Support:** Baseline newly available since 2024-07-09 (web-features `registered-custom-properties`). Chrome 85 / Firefox 128 / Safari 16.4.
- **See also:** [MDN: CSS @property](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@property)

### CS9. Existing state selector contract

- **Rule:** Follow the state selector contract in [web-markup-and-css.md Section 7](web-markup-and-css.md#7-css-architecture).
- **Why:** The web layer already owns how exposed state reaches CSS selectors, so this file does not define a second state source. See [A5](web-accessibility-patterns.md#a5-focus-visible-styling) for the visible keyboard focus rule.
- **When not to:** Use a class for a visual-only state that has no semantic state in the markup.
- **Pitfall:** A store-owned `.is-open` class can drift from the expanded state already present on the control.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [MDN: Attribute selectors](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Attribute_selectors)

---

| `:is()` and `:where()` | 88 | 82 | 14 | widely available since 2023-07-21 (web-features `is`); widely available since 2023-07-21 (web-features `where`) |
| `:has()` | 105 | 121 | 15.4 | widely available since 2026-06-19 (web-features `has`) |
| Native nesting | 120 | 117 | 17.2 | widely available since 2026-06-11 (web-features `nesting`) |
| `@scope` | 143 | 146 | 26.4 | newly available since 2026-03-24 (web-features `scope`) |
| `@property` | 85 | 128 | 16.4 | newly available since 2024-07-09 (web-features `registered-custom-properties`) |

# Web Layout and Sizing

This file keeps the deeper CSS layout mechanics.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

It covers stacking contexts, containing blocks, intrinsic sizing, grid tracks, containers and scrolling behavior.

### When to Use

- Changing how a fixed, sticky or stacked element is positioned.
- Sizing flex or grid tracks, or a container query, around intrinsic content.
- Handling media ratio, scrollbar space, scroll chaining or viewport height units.
- Adding a content-sized control or an intrinsic-size animation.

### Boundaries

- **Baseline flow and responsive rules.** The baseline flow and responsive rules remain in [web-markup-and-css.md](web-markup-and-css.md).

---

## 2. STACKING AND CONTAINING BLOCKS

### L1. Ancestors that capture fixed positioning

- **Rule:** Keep transforms, filters, perspective, paint or layout containment, relevant `will-change` values and `container-type` off ancestors of viewport-fixed headers or bars.
- **Why:** These properties can make an ancestor the containing block for a fixed descendant, so the descendant moves with that ancestor instead of the viewport. Transform, filter and containment behavior is longstanding.
- **When not to:** Scope a fixed child to an ancestor only when it is meant to remain fixed inside that component.
- **Pitfall:** Adding `will-change: transform` to smooth an ancestor can silently change where a fixed child is positioned.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2025-08-14 (web-features `container-queries`). Chrome 105 / Firefox 110 / Safari 16.
- **See also:** [MDN: CSS containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Containing_block)

### L2. Stacking context triggers

- **Rule:** Inspect the ancestor chain for a stacking context before increasing a `z-index` value.
- **Why:** A stacking context is painted as one unit, so a descendant cannot out-rank content in a different context. Triggers include the root, positioned elements with non-auto `z-index`, fixed or sticky positioning, flex or grid items with `z-index`, opacity below one, blend modes, `transform`, `translate`, `rotate`, `scale`, filters, perspective, clipping, masks, `isolation: isolate`, `contain: layout`, `contain: paint`, `contain: strict`, `contain: content`, `container-type`, `content-visibility: auto` and `will-change` naming one of these properties. Top-layer elements paint above ordinary stacking contexts.
- **When not to:** Raise a local `z-index` when the elements already share the same stacking context and the order alone is wrong.
- **Pitfall:** An opacity such as `0.999` creates a stacking context, while `isolation: isolate` creates one without changing opacity or clipping paint.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [MDN: CSS stacking context](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_positioned_layout/Stacking_context)

### L3. Flow root without clipping

- **Rule:** Use `display: flow-root` to contain floats or stop margin collapse when clipping is not required.
- **Why:** A flow root establishes a block formatting context without turning overflow into a clipping or scrolling rule.
- **When not to:** Use an overflow value when clipping is an intentional part of the component.
- **Pitfall:** `overflow: hidden` can clip content and prevent sticky descendants from sticking to their scrollport.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [MDN: CSS block formatting context](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_display/Block_formatting_context)

---

## 3. INTRINSIC AND GRID SIZING

### L4. Automatic minimum on flex and grid items

- **Rule:** Set `min-width: 0` or `min-inline-size: 0` on a flex or grid child that must shrink below its min-content size.
- **Why:** The automatic minimum can preserve the longest unbreakable content width, so the item refuses to shrink to the available track.
- **When not to:** Keep the automatic minimum when the item's content must set a lower bound on its track.
- **Pitfall:** Setting `overflow: hidden` may hide the overflow while leaving the sizing constraint in place.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [MDN: CSS min-width](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/min-width)

### L5. Grid tracks, subgrid and auto repetition

- **Rule:** Use `minmax(0, 1fr)` when long content must not widen a flexible track, use subgrid when nested items must share parent tracks, and choose `auto-fit` or `auto-fill` by whether empty tracks should collapse.
- **Why:** A bare `1fr` has an automatic minimum. Subgrid reuses the parent grid tracks. `auto-fit` collapses empty repeated tracks, while `auto-fill` preserves them.
- **When not to:** Keep the intrinsic minimum when content must determine the track size, or use independent tracks when nested columns should not align with the parent.
- **Pitfall:** One unbreakable string can widen a grid whose flexible track still has an automatic minimum.
- **Support:** Judgment, no version gate.
- **See also:** [MDN: CSS subgrid](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_grid_layout/Subgrid)

- **Rule:** Put query containment on a wrapper and query from its descendants, then use container units such as `cqi` or `cqw` where sizing should follow that wrapper.
- **Why:** A query container cannot use its own size query to style itself. `container-type: inline-size` also establishes containment that can affect fixed descendants and stacking.
- **When not to:** Use a viewport media query when the layout decision depends on the viewport rather than the component's available size.
- **Pitfall:** Adding `container-type` to the styled component itself does not make that component respond to its own size.
- **Support:** Baseline widely available since 2025-08-14 (web-features `container-queries`). Chrome 105 / Firefox 110 / Safari 16.
- **See also:** [MDN: CSS container size and style queries](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_containment/Container_size_and_style_queries)

### L7. Intrinsic media ratio

- **Rule:** Keep an image's or video's intrinsic `width` and `height` attributes consistent with its CSS `aspect-ratio`.
